title: AdRequest
name: dev.uap.supply.ad_request
description: The request body a serving node sends to an exchange to fill one or more placements on a generated turn. Sent only in the hosted and hybrid decisioning profiles; Profile L makes no request at all.
$comment:
Field-for-field mappable onto an OpenRTB 2.6 BidRequest so existing demand can bid with a translation layer rather than a rewrite. Each member names its OpenRTB equivalent. Where UAP has no equivalent the reason is an invariant, not an oversight:

  BidRequest.site / .app     no addressable page exists; replaced by `inference`
  BidRequest.device          almost every member is a fingerprinting vector; see `surface`
  BidRequest.user            no cross-session identifier may exist at all (I1)
  Imp.banner / .video        creative is structured data, not a rendered size

See SPEC.md Appendix C for the full mapping table.

id.description: Unique identifier for this request, generated by the node.
id.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `id`. UUIDv7 RECOMMENDED so the exchange can order requests without a separate timestamp.

test.description: 1 marks a test request that MUST NOT be billed.

integrity.description: The node's commitment to the organic answer, made before the auction runs.
integrity.$comment:
This is what turns answer integrity from an assertion into a proof. The exchange records the digest before a winner exists, so an answer matching it demonstrably did not depend on the auction outcome. A receipt whose rendered answer does not match the commitment is not billable.

Only the digest is sent. The answer text itself never leaves the node, so this adds no context egress.

Local decisioning has no round trip and therefore cannot produce this ordering proof. There the guarantee rests on deterministic composition, which anyone can recompute, on the holdout comparison, and at trust tier 2 on an attestation covering the enforcement path. SPEC.md §9.3 prices the difference rather than pretending it does not exist.

organic_answer_digest.description: Digest of the completed answer, computed before this request was built.

holdout_eligible.description: Whether this request may be selected as an integrity holdout.
holdout_eligible.$comment: A node that opts out of holdouts forfeits the only evidence that its served and unserved answers come from the same distribution, and exchanges MAY price it accordingly.

placements.description: The slots to fill. At least one is required.

inference.description: What produced the turn: the model, its steward, and the serving stack.

surface.description: The rendering environment, described only to the extent that does not identify a device.

context.description: The bounded, conversation-derived signal. Absent means untargeted inventory.

session.description: Turn position within the current conversation. Node-scoped and non-durable.

placement_id.description: Identifier for this slot, unique within the request.

tag_id.description: The seller's own identifier for this inventory unit.
tag_id.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `imp.tagid`. Buyers use it to build placement-level allow and block lists, which is how they exclude a single bad slot without excluding a whole seller.

floor_cpm_micros.description: Minimum acceptable clearing price for this placement.
floor_cpm_micros.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `imp.bidfloor`, expressed in micros rather than a floating-point currency unit.

deals.description: Pre-negotiated arrangements available on this placement.

private_auction.description: 1 restricts this placement to the listed deals.

expires_in_s.description: Seconds within which the winning creative must be rendered.
expires_in_s.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `imp.exp`. Bounds how long the decision nonce stays open.

metrics.description: Seller-supplied performance predictions for this placement.
metrics.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `imp.metric[]`. A buyer bidding CPC needs a click-through prediction it did not compute itself; without one it must discount every unfamiliar seller uniformly, which prices good supply the same as bad.

vendor.description: Source of the prediction. Absent means the seller itself.

inference.description: Replaces OpenRTB `site` and `app`. The unit of supply is a model turn, so the model is the inventory.
inference.$comment: This object is what a buyer applies suitability policy against. On the open web that decision is made on a domain; here there is no domain, and the closest equivalent is which model produced the text the ad sits beside.

model_id.description: Identifier of the model serving the turn.

weights_digest.description: Digest of the weights in use, where the operator can attest to it.

steward_id.description: Entity whose /.well-known/uap-model governs monetisation of this model.
steward_id.$comment: The exchange MUST fetch and honour that policy and MUST refuse to clear an auction that violates it. See SPEC.md §7.5.

quantization.description: Quantization applied to the weights, where known.

supply_agent_id.description: Aggregator holding the commercial account, where one exists.

trust_tier.description: Tier asserted by this supply. Verified at settlement, not at request time.

surface.description: Replaces OpenRTB `device`. Every member is a closed enumeration.
surface.$comment: OpenRTB `device` carries ua, ip, ifa, model, make, and a screen geometry, which together identify a device even without a cookie. None of that may appear here. What remains is what a buyer genuinely needs to render correctly and nothing that narrows the audience below the k floor.

locale.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `device.language`, restricted to language and region.

geo.description: Coarse location. Country granularity is the default and the maximum for most deployments.
geo.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `device.geo`, less lat, lon, ipservice, and everything below region. `biometric_precise_location` is a suppressing category in the sensitive taxonomy.

attested.description: Whether the surface runs an attested build. Substantiated at settlement.

session.description: Position within the current conversation. Contains no identifier of any kind.
session.$comment: OpenRTB `user` has no equivalent here and cannot have one: I1 forbids any identifier stable across sessions, including a hash. The consequence is stated plainly rather than hidden. Frequency capping is enforceable only within a single serving node, because only the node can correlate turns, and it never transmits what it used to do so. A buyer reading a frequency cap in a campaign bundle should read it as per-node, not network-wide.

ads_shown_this_conversation.description: How many placements this conversation has already carried. Lets a buyer decline to add to a crowded turn.

mechanism.description: Pricing rule the exchange will apply.
mechanism.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `at`, where 1 is first price and 2 is second price.

currency.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `cur[]`, restricted to one value: UAP performs no conversion.

timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds the node will wait before treating the request as a no-fill.
timeout_ms.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `tmax`. The serve-time budget is p99 under 80 ms measured exchange-side. A node MUST treat a timeout as a no-fill and render nothing, never a placeholder that later swaps in.

objective.description: What the seller expects demand to optimise for on this request.
objective.$comment: Aligned with the objectives the market already buys against: reach prices on CPM, clicks on CPC, conversions on CPA. Trust tier 0 supply MUST NOT be sold on reach.

policy.description: Seller-side restrictions the exchange MUST apply before ranking.

blocked_advertisers.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `badv`, matched on advertiser domain.

category_taxonomy.description: Taxonomy the category values are drawn from.

brand_suitability.description: Maximum acceptable risk per GARM content category.
brand_suitability.$comment: The GARM Brand Safety Floor and Suitability Framework is the vocabulary advertisers already write their media plans in. A single low, medium, high field cannot express 'no adjacency to firearms at any level, medium tolerance for debated social issues', which is what a real plan says.

transaction_id.description: Identifier shared by every hop handling this impression opportunity.
transaction_id.$comment: Maps to OpenRTB `source.tid`. Lets a buyer detect the same opportunity arriving by several paths and bid once.

final_decision.description: 1 when this exchange makes the final selection, 0 when it is one of several.

payment_chain.description: Ordered list of entities in the payment path.
